text.p: Estonia has been plunged into a fresh political crisis after the country's junior coalition partner walked out of the government.
The small Baltic state must now seek its seventh government since winning independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991, after the Reform Party quit the coalition on Thursday.
The party was furious with Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi after his Coalition Party signed a wide-ranging cooperation deal with the leading opposition party.
The deal was a huge slap in the face to the Reform Party, prompting it to end the alliance with the Coalitionists.
Vaehi's spokespeople were quick to give assurances that political change would not threaten the economic reforms that Estonia, the smallest of the Baltic states, has pursued since independence.
After a near three-hour meeting and last-minute talks with President Lennart Meri, the Reform Party council voted overwhelmingly to leave the government.
"We could not find any other way out of the crisis even after meeting the president," Reform Party leader and outgoing foreign minister, Siim Kallas, told journalists.
The Reform Party had demanded that Vaehi scrap his cooperation deal with the leading opposition Centre Party.
The Reformists said the deal could lead to policies that were too friendly to huge neighbour Russia, which many Estonians fear wants to bring them back under its control.
Russia ruled Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania for most of the last 200 years and all three Baltic states look with bitterness on the 50 years they were unwilling Soviet citizens.
Vaehi is now expected to hold talks with the Centre Party on forming a coalition in a rerun of the previous government.
The Reform Party says that a coalition with the Centre Party, seen as left-of-centre, would lead to slower reforms.
A government spokeswoman said Vaehi would always pursue market reforms and integration with the West when in power.
"All talk by the opposition about a turnaround is nonsense," a spokeswoman for Vaehi told Reuters.
"Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi will continue the policies he has pursued as prime minister, including close integration with the EU and joining Western defence structures," she added.
The former Coalition/Centre party government collapsed amid scandal after the Centre Party leader was found to have made recordings of confidential conversations with other politicians.
Vaehi can command 40 seats in the 101-seat parliament, composed of the Coalition Party's 19 seats and the 21 seats of a bloc of smaller rural parties with which he is in permanent alliance.
